docs.text: STAC API Protocol: A lightweight way to expose existing data ¶ STAC API Protocol enables existing data systems to become interoperable STAC API services without requiring them to adopt a new catalogue infrastructure. Since version 0.2.0, the protocol implementation supports the STAC API - Filter Extension Specification v1.0.0-rc.4 . The HTTP adapter handles CQL2 Text and CQL2 JSON requests, exposes queryables, and advertises Filter conformance. Service providers implement filter evaluation against their data. See the Filter Extension service contract for supported routes and provider requirements. Built around a clean separation between the HTTP protocol layer for STAC API Core , Collections , Features , and Item Search and the underlying data services, it provides the essential STAC API functionality while leaving data access, metadata mapping, and catalogue operations to pluggable implementations. This makes it particularly suited to building lightweight STAC facades over heterogeneous data sources, from legacy catalogues and REST services to databases, object storage, and custom scientific data systems. Rather than introducing another catalogue to maintain, STAC API Protocol allows existing systems to expose their data through a common, standards-based interface. Minimal footprint: Avoid unnecessary catalogue infrastructure, metadata duplication, and synchronization pipelines. Backend agnostic: Integrate heterogeneous data sources without imposing a common storage technology. Clean separation of concerns: Keep protocol handling independent from data access and business logic. Reusable deployment: Maintain one API implementation while deploying different service providers. Extensible integration: Adapt existing systems through small, dedicated service implementations. Interoperability by design: Make existing data accessible through the STAC ecosystem with minimal architectural changes. STAC API Protocol is designed for situations where the challenge is not building another catalogue, but making existing data discoverable and accessible through a standard interface. Ddeveloped according to Hexagonal Architecture (Ports and Adapters) and the separation of concerns associated with Clean Architecture : FastAPI acts exclusively as the HTTP adapter , separating the STAC API protocol layer from the underlying data access and implementation logic. Each source can have its own: Data model Metadata representation Query mechanism Identifier scheme Asset location Authentication mechanism Search capabilities and limitations The facade only needs to translate these capabilities into the STAC API contract. The provider is discovered through a fixed entry-point contract, and the deployed environment supplies the implementation. This brings some important practical benefits: No environment-specific forks of the API application. No backend-specific logic in the protocol layer. Simpler deployment packaging because the provider can be a separate Python distribution. Better maintainability because protocol upgrades and data-source implementations evolve independently. Reuse across organizations and infrastructures, even when the underlying systems differ substantially. This is particularly compelling for organizations operating several data platforms with different technologies, interfaces, or metadata schemas. This makes stac-api-protocol particularly useful when the objective is to wrap existing data services, not build another centralized metadata database. A better fit for federation and distributed infrastructures ¶ This architecture also aligns naturally with distributed catalogue environments. Instead of forcing every data provider to consolidate its metadata into a central catalogue, each provider can expose its own STAC API facade. A higher-level discovery service can then federate or aggregate those interfaces. This allows you to preserve: Data sovereignty; Existing operational boundaries; Local access control policies; Technology diversity; Independent provider evolution. The STAC API becomes the common language between systems, rather than a requirement for all systems to share a common implementation. For distributed infrastructures, this is often a more natural model than centralizing metadata ownership. stac-fastapi is probably a good choice when: Your data already exists elsewhere. The source already provides some discovery or query capabilities. You want to avoid duplicating metadata. You need to map different data models into STAC. You want the smallest possible implementation between your data and STAC clients. You want a single reusable API deployment with interchangeable service providers. Its modularity and extension ecosystem are real advantages. Main advantages of stac-api-protocol ¶ There are architectural benefits of adopting the protocol/service separation: 1. Clear separation of concerns ¶ The protocol layer owns HTTP, routing, request validation, serialization, and protocol-level errors. The implementation owns data access, query translation, metadata mapping, and domain logic. 2. Backend-agnostic by design ¶ You are not required to adopt a specific storage technology or catalogue database. Existing systems remain the source of truth; STAC is the interoperability layer placed on top of them. 3. Minimal runtime and operational footprint ¶ A facade can avoid deploying and maintaining a dedicated STAC metadata database, ingestion pipeline, synchronization jobs, and indexing infrastructure when the underlying source already provides the information required. 4. Reuse the same API implementation ¶ The HTTP and STAC implementation can be reused across multiple deployments. Only the source-specific service implementation changes. 5. Pluggable service implementations ¶ Backend implementations can be installed independently and discovered at runtime, avoiding the need to fork or modify the API application for each deployment. 6. No forced data migration or duplication ¶ Metadata can be mapped on demand from the source system into STAC representations, reducing synchronization problems and the risk of maintaining multiple versions of the same catalogue information. 7. Independent lifecycle and deployment ¶ The facade can be deployed, upgraded, or replaced independently from the data source. It does not need to become the owner of the source's data or lifecycle. Documentation ¶ First service tutorial : build and run a minimal provider. Register a service factory : configure discovery and troubleshoot startup. Install and run : prepare the runtime environment. Service contract : methods, return values, and HTTP behavior. Architecture : understand the adapter boundary and dependency direction.

docs.title: Explanation

docs.text: Architecture: Ports and Adapters ¶ STAC API Protocol is developed according to Hexagonal Architecture (Ports and Adapters) . It follows the same separation of application behavior from delivery mechanisms emphasized by Clean Architecture . These are closely related architectural approaches; here their practical consequence is that FastAPI acts exclusively as the HTTP adapter . The service port ¶ StacApiService , defined in src/stac_api_protocol/stac_service.py , is the boundary between the HTTP adapter and an adopter's catalogue application. It is an abstract base class with five adopter-defined catalogue operations and two final metadata methods. Adopters subclass it and supply a catalogue identifier, title, and description. Incomplete subclasses cannot be instantiated. The shared landing-page method builds root-relative links. Catalogue search and retrieval operations remain independent of FastAPI request objects. The conformance method returns a fixed declaration of the bundled STAC and OGC classes, including Filter Extension capabilities since version 0.2.0. The adapter handles the Filter protocol; each adopter must implement the advertised filtering semantics. See the service contract . HTTP client | v FastAPI HTTP adapter (stac_api_protocol.main) | | calls the StacApiService port v Adopter's service implementation | v Application/domain logic and backend integrations | v Catalogue storage, search engine, or remote services This diagram shows request flow. The HTTP adapter depends on the service contract; it does not import a concrete adopter implementation. The adopter supplies that implementation at runtime through an installed Python entry point. Responsibilities ¶ Component Responsibility FastAPI HTTP adapter Route requests, parse and validate HTTP inputs, invoke the service, serialize results, and translate failures into HTTP responses. StacApiService port Define the operations and data types required by the adapter. Adopter's service Implement catalogue use cases, filtering, lookup, and result construction; coordinate domain logic and backend access. Adopter's backend integrations Access databases, indexes, files, or remote services as required by the application. Provider factory Construct or obtain a configured service and supply it to the HTTP adapter. Keep FastAPI responses and dependency injection out of your catalogue business logic. Service methods receive ordinary filter values and return the STAC objects specified by the port. If your domain uses different objects, map them to these types at the service boundary. The port intentionally uses PySTAC, GeoJSON, and package models; it is a STAC-facing contract, not a universal domain model. Runtime composition ¶ When stac_api_protocol.main is imported, load_dependency("item_service") looks up installed entry points in the stacapi.service group. It loads the unique matching callable. FastAPI then uses that callable through Depends to obtain the service for route execution. Discovery loads the factory; it does not call it to create a global service. Do not assume the adapter constructs a singleton or manages your backend's connection lifecycle. Your provider and deployment must choose the appropriate resource lifetime. A simple zero-argument factory is sufficient to get started. The loader checks that there is exactly one matching entry and that it is callable. It does not validate the returned object's implementation of the service contract. Type-check and test your implementation against the service contract. See factory registration for the exact metadata and the tutorial for a runnable example. Schema-first HTTP contracts ¶ The OpenAPI schema under schemas/ is the source of truth for generated API artifacts. Adopters should reuse the existing models and implement the service port instead of editing generated routes or models to attach a backend. Changes to schema-defined contracts belong in the schema and the repository's configured generation workflow.

docs.text: Install and run ¶ Use Python 3.11 or later. Install the HTTP adapter and an ASGI server in a virtual environment: python -m venv .venv source .venv/bin/activate python -m pip install stac-api-protocol uvicorn The adapter does not include a catalogue backend. Implement and register a service provider , then install that package in the same environment. From the provider's project directory: python -m pip install -e . python -m uvicorn stac_api_protocol.main:app --host 127 .0.0.1 --port 8000 The application discovers the provider at import time. Missing or ambiguous registrations prevent startup. Develop against a local adapter checkout ¶ From the stac-api-protocol repository root, install the adapter in editable mode: python -m pip install -e . Install your provider and ASGI server in that environment as well. The ASGI import path remains stac_api_protocol.main:app . Inspect the running API ¶ http://127.0.0.1:8000/ : catalogue landing page supplied by your service. http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs : FastAPI's interactive API documentation. http://127.0.0.1:8000/openapi.json : the runtime OpenAPI description. There is no stac_api_protocol command-line entry point. Run the application through an ASGI server.

docs.text: Register a service factory ¶ Implement the port ¶ Create a concrete implementation of StacApiService from stac_api_protocol.stac_service . Implement the five abstract methods in the service contract , using your own application and backend logic. The tutorial provides a complete minimal example. Export the factory ¶ In your adopter package, expose a callable that returns the configured service: # my_catalogue/provider.py from stac_api_protocol.stac_service import StacApiService from .service import CatalogueService def create_service () -> StacApiService : """Provide the catalogue implementation used by the HTTP adapter.""" return CatalogueService ( id = "catalogue" , title = "Catalogue" , description = "Catalogue data" ) This example uses the base constructor, which requires catalogue identity metadata. Adapt construction to your application's configuration and resource lifecycle. The inherited landing-page method uses the incoming request; your five catalogue operations receive ordinary filter values. Declare the entry point ¶ Add this table to the adopter package's pyproject.toml : [project.entry-points. "stacapi.service" ] item_service = "my_catalogue.provider:create_service" Part Meaning stacapi.service Entry-point group queried by this adapter. item_service Required entry name for the service covering all supported routes. my_catalogue.provider Importable module in your installed package. create_service Callable factory exported by that module. Use the callable's name without parentheses. Despite its name, item_service serves landing-page, collection, conformance, and item operations alike. Install and verify discovery ¶ From your adopter project directory, install the package into the same environment that runs the ASGI server: python -m pip install -e . Reinstall after changing entry-point metadata, and restart the server. Merely placing the module on PYTHONPATH does not install entry-point metadata. Inspect registrations without starting the application: from importlib.metadata import entry_points for entry in entry_points ( group = "stacapi.service" , name = "item_service" ): print ( entry . name , entry . value ) There must be exactly one match. Start the adapter only after installing it: python -m uvicorn stac_api_protocol.main:app --host 127 .0.0.1 --port 8000 Install Uvicorn separately as described in Install and run . Troubleshoot startup ¶ Failure What to check Missing required dependency: item_service Install your provider in the server environment; check both the group and entry name. Multiple implementations found for: item_service Use an environment with only one matching provider registration. There is no automatic priority selection. Dependency is not callable: item_service Point at a factory function or another callable, rather than a prebuilt non-callable instance. Import failure while loading the entry point Check the module path and install your provider's runtime dependencies. Import errors propagate. Failure when a request invokes the service Check factory construction and whether the returned service implements the service contract. Discovery alone does not check these.

docs.text: Reference ¶ Adopters provide the application behavior by implementing StacApiService , the service port defined in src/stac_api_protocol/stac_service.py . Your service connects catalogue operations to your domain logic, storage, and search systems. This package supplies the routes, request validation, response serialization, and HTTP error handling. Integration at a glance ¶ Subclass StacApiService and implement its five abstract catalogue operations. Expose a callable factory that returns your service implementation. Register that factory in your package's pyproject.toml : [project.entry-points. "stacapi.service" ] item_service = "my_catalogue.provider:create_service" Install your package alongside stac-api-protocol , then serve stac_api_protocol.main:app with an ASGI server. The entry-point group stacapi.service and entry name item_service are required. The module and factory names on the right-hand side are yours to choose. Exactly one installed provider must match. Installing this HTTP adapter alone does not supply a catalogue backend. One application, multiple interchangeable providers ¶ The protocol defines a StacApiService contract, while implementations provide the actual catalogue behavior. The service factory is registered using Python entry points, so the HTTP application can remain independent of the provider implementation. For example, the same application could be deployed with different providers and the application itself does not need to know which implementation is deployed. Service contract documents the StacApiService operations, their HTTP routes, result semantics, and provider discovery.

docs.text: Service contract ¶ Adopters subclass StacApiService , defined in src/stac_api_protocol/stac_service.py . The HTTP adapter invokes its synchronous methods with parsed filter values. All seven operations belong to the same registered item_service provider. The constructor requires id , title , and description . Five catalogue operations are abstract. get_landing_page() and get_conformance_declaration() are final concrete methods and must not be overridden. The landing page uses root-relative links. Both responses advertise the bundled STAC and OGC conformance classes, including Filter Extension capabilities since version 0.2.0. Operations and routes ¶ HTTP route Service method Return type GET / get_landing_page() LandingPage GET /collections get_collections() Collections GET /collections/{collectionId} describe_collection(collection_id) pystac.Collection or None GET /collections/{collectionId}/items get_features(collection_id, limit, bbox, datetime, filter) pystac.ItemCollection or None GET /collections/{collectionId}/items/{featureId} get_feature(collection_id, feature_id) pystac.Item or None GET /conformance get_conformance_declaration() ConformanceClasses GET /search , POST /search get_item_search(bbox, intersects, datetime, limit, ids, collections, filter) pystac.ItemCollection or None GET /queryables Served by the HTTP adapter JSON Schema ( application/schema+json ) GET /collections/{collectionId}/queryables Adapter checks describe_collection(collection_id) JSON Schema ( application/schema+json ) LandingPage , Collections , and ConformanceClasses come from stac_api_protocol.models . Use these existing types rather than creating parallel representations of the HTTP contract. Filter Extension support since 0.2.0 ¶ Version 0.2.0 introduced protocol-level support for the STAC API - Filter Extension Specification v1.0.0-rc.4 . Request Filter representation Default filter-lang GET /search and GET /collections/{collectionId}/items filter query parameter containing CQL2 Text or JSON-encoded CQL2 JSON cql2-text POST /search filter JSON body field containing a CQL2 JSON expression or a CQL2 Text string cql2-json Use filter-lang to select cql2-text or cql2-json . The supported filter-crs is http://www.opengis.net/def/crs/OGC/1.3/CRS84 . Queryables are exposed at both catalogue and collection scope, with discovery links in the landing page and collection metadata. Collection queryables return HTTP 404 for an unknown collection. The adapter validates CQL2 JSON structure and delegates the expression to the provider. CQL2 Text is forwarded unchanged. Since 0.2.0, provider implementations of get_features and get_item_search must accept a filter argument typed as str | dict[str, object] | bool | None : text, a parsed JSON expression, a boolean predicate, or no filter. docs.text: Adopters subclass StacApiService , defined in src/stac_api_protocol/stac_service.py . The HTTP adapter invokes its synchronous methods with parsed filter values. All seven operations belong to the same registered item_service provider. The constructor requires id , title , and description . Five catalogue operations are abstract. get_landing_page() and get_conformance_declaration() are final concrete methods and must not be overridden. The landing page uses root-relative links. Both responses advertise the bundled STAC and OGC conformance classes, including Filter Extension capabilities since version 0.2.0.

docs.text: Build your first service ¶ This tutorial builds an empty catalogue provider. It demonstrates the five abstract operations of the service contract and factory discovery without requiring a database. An empty catalogue cannot demonstrate filtering or item retrieval; replace these methods with your own application logic when connecting real data. 1. Create an adopter package ¶ Create this layout in a separate directory: my-catalogue/ ├── pyproject.toml └── src/ └── my_catalogue/ ├── __init__.py └── provider.py Leave __init__.py empty. Put the following in pyproject.toml : [build-system] requires = [ "hatchling" ] build-backend = "hatchling.build" [project] name = "my-catalogue" version = "0.1.0" requires-python = ">=3.11" dependencies = [ "stac-api-protocol" ] [project.entry-points. "stacapi.service" ] item_service = "my_catalogue.provider:create_service" [tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel] packages = [ "src/my_catalogue" ] The entry point belongs to your adopter package. It tells the HTTP adapter where to find your factory once this package is installed. 2. Implement the service port ¶ Put this implementation in src/my_catalogue/provider.py : from geojson import GeometryCollection from geojson.geometry import Geometry from pystac import Collection , Item , ItemCollection from stac_api_protocol.models import Collections from stac_api_protocol.stac_service import StacApiService class EmptyCatalogueService ( StacApiService ): """Expose an empty catalogue to demonstrate the service boundary.""" def get_collections ( self ) -> Collections : """Return the catalogue's empty collection listing.""" return Collections ( collections = [], links = []) def describe_collection ( self , collection_id : str ) -> Collection | None : """Report that the requested collection does not exist.""" return None def get_features ( self , collection_id : str , limit : int | None , bbox : list [ float ] | None , datetime : str | None , ) -> ItemCollection | None : """Report that the requested collection does not exist.""" return None def get_feature ( self , collection_id : str , feature_id : str ) -> Item | None : """Report that the requested item does not exist.""" return None def get_item_search ( self , bbox : list [ float ] | None , intersects : Geometry | GeometryCollection | None , datetime : str | None , limit : int | None , ids : list [ str ] | None , collections : list [ str ] | None , ) -> ItemCollection | None : """Return a successful search with no matching items.""" return ItemCollection ([]) def create_service () -> StacApiService : """Provide an empty catalogue service to the HTTP adapter.""" return EmptyCatalogueService ( id = "empty-catalogue" , title = "Empty catalogue" , description = "An empty demonstration catalogue" ) The class specializes StacApiService ; the factory returns it through the port. Neither needs to import FastAPI. All HTTP handling remains in the adapter. The base class supplies the final landing-page and conformance methods. It builds links from the incoming landing-page request and advertises the four bundled STAC API conformance classes. Adopters implement the other five abstract operations and must fulfill those advertised capabilities. This empty example demonstrates the integration mechanics; it is not a conformance certification. 3. Install and serve ¶ From my-catalogue/ , create an environment and install your package and server: python -m venv .venv source .venv/bin/activate python -m pip install -e . uvicorn python -m uvicorn stac_api_protocol.main:app --host 127 .0.0.1 --port 8000 Installation records the entry-point metadata. On application import, the adapter finds item_service in the stacapi.service group and loads create_service . FastAPI invokes the provider as a dependency when serving requests. 4. Exercise the adapter ¶ In another terminal: curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/ curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/collections curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/search curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8000/collections/missing Expect a catalogue landing page, an empty collection listing, an empty GeoJSON FeatureCollection, and an HTTP 404 for the missing collection. You can also try these requests in http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs . 5. Connect your application ¶ Replace EmptyCatalogueService with your concrete service implementation. Keep its method signatures compatible with the service contract , apply the supplied filters in your application, and return the required STAC objects. Update the factory to construct your configured implementation. The HTTP adapter and its route definitions do not need to change.
